eds-theme-color-background-visualization: Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 1. Use sparingly; not for series fills, bands or row tints.
First categorical series fill for unordered groups in charts. Take categorical slots in order, starting here. Also the called-out mark when one mark is highlighted against the rest.
Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 2. Use sparingly; not for series fills, bands or row tints.
Second categorical series fill. Use only when slot 1 is already in use.
Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 3. Neutral rather than green so it does not read as a twin of slot 1's tint. Use sparingly.
Third categorical series fill. Use only when slots 1 and 2 are already in use.
Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 4. Use sparingly; not for series fills, bands or row tints.
Fourth categorical series fill. Light; give thin lines and small points extra weight. Shares a primitive with the warning high-emphasis background, so keep warning Tags out of plot areas that use it.
Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 5. Use sparingly; not for series fills, bands or row tints.
Fifth categorical series fill. Use only when slots 1 through 4 are already in use.
Tint for a Tag that labels categorical slot 6. Use sparingly; not for series fills, bands or row tints.
Sixth categorical series fill. Use only when slots 1 through 5 are already in use.
Seventh categorical series fill. Light; give thin lines and small points extra weight. No low-emphasis value.
Eighth and last categorical series fill. Light; give thin lines and small points extra weight. No low-emphasis value. Past eight series, use direct labels or pattern fills rather than more color.
Overflow bucket for series beyond the eighth, and the context marks when one mark is called out. Never a ninth identity the reader is expected to remember.
The zeroth scalar value
Lowest non-zero bin of a scalar scale. Bin data to four steps; do not interpolate.
Second of four scalar bins.
Third of four scalar bins.
Highest of four scalar bins.
A measured value of zero on a scalar (magnitude) scale. Not for missing data, which is shown as no fill plus a dash.
The reference value of a divergent scale: the target, the plan, or no change. Anchor here, not at the median of the data.
Just below the reference value on a divergent scale.
Second step below the reference value on a divergent scale.
Furthest below the reference value on a divergent scale.
Just above the reference value on a divergent scale.
Second step above the reference value on a divergent scale.
Furthest above the reference value on a divergent scale.
